names.note: Her own name, read out of doxologia.ro's line for 4 iunie, «Sfintele Mironosițe Maria și Marta, surorile Dreptului Lazăr», which names two women.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 4 Ιουνίου, «Αγίες Μάρθα και Μαρία οι αδελφές του Λαζάρου», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 4. јун ст. ст., „Свете Марта и Марија“, which names the two sisters and nothing else. Свете is not a rank, so there is nothing to strip and the bare personal name is the whole of the form. THE FOLD IS DELIBERATE: `foldchk.py` returns `[('mary-called-marinos', 'sr'), ('mary-of-tarsus', 'sr'), ('mary-wife-of-xenophon', 'sr')]`, so this is the fourth holder of the commonest woman’s name there is. The heading offers nothing fuller: the sisterhood is in the body, not in the heading, and §6 does not let a form be built out of a body.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 4 iunie — «Sfintele Mironosițe Maria și Marta, surorile Dreptului Lazăr»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Ιουνίου — «Αγίες Μάρθα και Μαρία οι αδελφές του Λαζάρου»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day as the folder's Romanian row, and it carries both sisters on one page with a head line each. They are plainly the same two: the sisters of Lazarus at Bethany. Two hymns are taken and both stand in both folders, because both name both sisters. The page prints three further texts — a μεγαλυνάριον, an οἶκος and a κάθισμα — which are not taken, because the schema holds a troparion and a kontakion and nothing else; the κάθισμα is the one that distinguishes the sisters, saying that the one prepared food for him in faith while the other anointed him with myrrh and wiped the Lord's feet with the hair of her head. The page gives no year for either of them and no place but Bethany, so no `dates` object is added and `locations` is left out.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 17.06.2026 (4. јун ст. ст.) — „Свете Марта и Марија“

attestations.note: The day’s sixth and last entry, which names her second of two. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. THE SHORTEST ENTRY OF THE DAY AND IT CORROBORATES THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS ON THIS FOLDER. Four sentences: sisters of Lazarus; after the Lord’s ascension Lazarus went to preach the Gospel; in this his sisters helped him; „Не зна се где су скончале“ — it is not known where they ended. **That last sentence is why `dates` and `locations` are both absent here, and a third book stating it outright is worth more to this folder than a new scene would be**: doxologia says the same in its three sentences, and saint.gr says only that the sisters were counted worthy to die peacefully and not under persecution. No year, no place, from any of the three. `dates` AND `locations` DELIBERATELY STILL ABSENT, AND THE LIFE CARRIES NO DIGITS so that no sentence of it can put a year beside an end this corpus does not record. `types` STILL EMPTY, AND THAT IS A READING TOO. Свете is not a rank and this heading has no other word in it. doxologia’s day line calls the two «Sfintele Mironosițe» and saint.gr’s kathisma calls them deacons of Christ; **myrrh-bearer is not in the `types` vocabulary at all**, `deaconess` would be written on a hymn and not on a life, and this book gives neither word. So the folder keeps no type, as it has since it was made. `related` UNTOUCHED: the sister and the brother are both already there, and this entry names no one else. THE FOLD IS DELIBERATE: `foldchk.py` returns `[('mary-called-marinos', 'sr'), ('mary-of-tarsus', 'sr'), ('mary-wife-of-xenophon', 'sr')]`, so this is the fourth holder of the commonest woman’s name there is. The heading offers nothing fuller: the sisterhood is in the body, not in the heading, and §6 does not let a form be built out of a body. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Τῷ Σωτῆρι ἀμέμπτως διακονήσασαι, αἱ τοῦ Ἁγίου Λαζάρου θεῖαι αὐτάδελφοι, σὺν τῇ Μάρθᾳ τῇ κλεινῇ, Μαρία πάνσεμνε, καὶ τὴν Ἀνάστασιν Αὐτοῦ, σὺν Μυροφόροις Γυναιξί, μαθοῦσαι ἐκ τοῦ Ἀγγέλου, φωτὸς ἐμπλήσθητε θείου, ἡμῖν αἰτοῦσαι τὰ σωτήρια.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α´, Τὸν Συνάναρχον Λόγον, on the page of the two sisters; it names them both, which is why it stands in both folders

english.text: Having served the Saviour blamelessly, O divine sisters of holy Lazarus — renowned Martha and all-revered Mary — and having learned of his Resurrection from the angel together with the myrrh-bearing women, you were filled with divine light. Ask for us the things that bring salvation.

hymns.text: Τῶν ἀδελφῶν τὴν δυάδα τὴν πάντιμον, τὰς τοῦ Λαζάρου συγγόνους τιμήσωμεν, Μαρίαν καὶ Μάρθαν ἐν ᾄσμασιν, ὡς ἂν αὐτῶν ἱκεσίαις πρὸς Κύριον, πταισμάτων συγχώρησιν λάβωμεν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β´, Τοῖς τῶν αἱμάτων σου, on the page of the two sisters; it names them both

english.text: Let us honour in song the all-honoured pair of sisters, the kinswomen of Lazarus, Mary and Martha, that by their entreaties to the Lord we may receive forgiveness of our offences.
